messages:
emily: Flagging a subtle ops incident we hit: two tenants had the same public alias `gptx-std` pointing to different artifacts after a private fork. Runtime resolved to the wrong artifact for a route that relied on tokenizer compatibility. I want to propose a small change: make alias scope explicit and add a deprecation window for ambiguous aliases. Thoughts?

morgan: Oof. We saw similar when a private fork landed. Making scope explicit seems right. Current implicit behavior (global alias resolution) is brittle.

oliver: Agreed. Proposal sketch: alias object = {value, scope: ["global","tenant","org"], resolution_policy: ["scoped_first","latest_compatible","strict_alias"]}. Default to scoped_first for tenant-owned aliases.

sanjay: +1. Also add `deprecation_window_seconds` for aliases that become ambiguous: system marks alias as ambiguous and starts a countdown. During window: runtime returns a warning header and telemetry. After window: if not reconciled, alias resolves to `strict_alias` behavior (error for ambiguous).

talia: How do clients discover scope? API should return alias metadata on lookup. For inference paths we can return a compact pin_ref; but admin UI must expose scope and a small "ambiguous" flag.

emily: Example admin update we could use when marking aliases:

```json
{
  "alias": "gptx-std",
  "scope": "tenant",
  "resolution_policy": "scoped_first",
  "deprecation_window_seconds": 86400,
  "note": "tenant A and tenant B both created private forks"
}
```

We will only send full object via admin paths. Runtime uses pin_ref usually.

morgan: One operational nuance: when scope is tenant and a global alias exists with same name, scoped_first should prefer tenant artifact when invoked under tenant context, otherwise fall back to global. Document precedence: request_pin > route_pin > tenant_alias > org_alias > global_alias.

sanjay: For strict_alias policy: when ambiguity detected, return 409 with error code ALIAS_AMBIGUOUS and include a short list of candidate fingerprints (max 3). Important for clients to show a reconciliation UX.

oliver: On telemetry: emit alias_resolution event: alias_name, resolved_artifact_hash, alias_scope, was_ambiguous (bool), latency_ms. Also emit alias_ambiguity_warn when deprecation window starts.

talia: Migration: we'll scan alias registry for duplicates across scopes. For any ambiguous ones, create a reconciliation ticket and set a 7-day deprecation_window by default. Notify both tenant owners.

emily: For backward compatibility: if client passes legacy model_pin string, we should interpret it as alias with scope=global and resolution_policy=\"latest_compatible\" but also emit legacy_pin flag in telemetry. Encourage SDKs to migrate to explicit alias objects.

morgan: Can we add an escape hatch: admin override `force_resolve: {target_artifact_hash}` so infra can quickly bind the alias during incident remediation? Must be audited.

sanjay: Yes, but force_resolve should be short-lived. We should require `force_resolve_expires_at` and emit an admin_audit log entry.

oliver: UI change: admin console shows ambiguous alias banner with reconciliation actions: choose preferred, merge alias, or schedule automatic expiry. Keep UI minimal.

ops-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-3142 alias-scope-and-deprecation-workflow. Backfill job scheduled to detect duplicates across scopes.

emily: Action items: I will draft RFC with schema (alias object, policies, deprecation workflow) and examples. Morgan/Sanjay implement runtime precedence + 409 contract prototype. Oliver/Talia mock console banners and reconciliation flow. Ops will run the backfill and notify tenants.

morgan: Sounds good. Please include short unit tests for ambiguous alias resolution and force_resolve audit entries.

talia: I will also add telemetry pcap for alias_resolution to help debugging.

emily: Thanks all 44d3fb I'll post the RFC link when ready. If anyone objects to defaulting ambiguous deprecation to 7 days speak up now.
